author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Rescue crews in Nepal are racing to reach hundreds of workers believed trapped in tunnels at a hydropower project after catastrophic flooding. 
Tunnel engineering professor Arnold Dix, who helped rescue 41 Indian workers from a Himalayan tunnel collapse in 2023, told Al Jazeera the operation is unlike any rescue he has ever seen, with rocks "the size of cars" blocking the way. 
He said crews have found the tunnel entrance, established drainage and are using explosives to clear massive boulders — a rare and risky approach in a rescue operation. 
Dix described a "Goldilocks zone" inside the power station where conditions, including air, water and possibly food, may sustain life. 
He said there is "every chance" that people could still be alive inside. Dix praised the resilience of Nepalese workers and said rescuers are doing everything possible to reach the area where survivors may be sheltering.

At least 150 people are reported dead and thousands remain missing after devastating flash floods in Nepal and China’s Tibet region.

International rescue teams have joined the search for survivors in underground tunnels at hydropower projects in Nepal, where hundreds of workers are believed to remain trapped.

Specialist teams and equipment from China, India and South Korea are assisting Nepalese crews with search and rescue operations. Forensic experts from China and Singapore are also expected to help identify recovered remains.

In China’s Tibet region, rescue teams have reached areas previously cut off by damaged roads and begun using heavy machinery to search for those still unaccounted for.

The disaster has also raised concerns about dangerous glacial lakes in the Himalayas and the possibility of further glacial flood events. Nepal’s government says rebuilding affected communities could cost billions of dollars.

Germany has formally accused Russia of being behind the drone incident at Leipzig Airport and is responding with a series of measures aimed at increasing pressure on Moscow. Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul says the Russian Consulate-General in Bonn will close on 18 September, while the lease for the Russian House of Science and Culture in Berlin will also be terminated. Berlin is proposing further EU measures against individuals linked to alleged Russian hybrid attacks, tightening entry controls for Russian nationals and increasing pressure on Russia's shadow fleet. Germany has stopped short of expelling Russian diplomats, but the measures are being presented as a clear signal that Berlin is serious about responding to Moscow and wants stronger action from the European Union. 

Al Jazeera's Dominic Kane reports from Berlin.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema has been sworn in for a second term after winning last month's presidential election with about 60 percent of the vote. His main rival, opposition leader Brian Mundubile, received around 38 percent but is in prison on treason charges, which he denies. Mundubile and his running mate, Makebi Zulu, are accused of planning an armed insurgency to disrupt the election and say they are ready to defend themselves in court. Regional and international election observers have reported serious irregularities, including alleged interference with vote counting, soldiers deployed at polling stations and the closure of courts. Hichilema came to power in 2021 promising a democratic break from the previous government, which he accused of rigging elections and jailing opponents. As Zambia seeks investment in its copper and other mineral resources, the government's treatment of political opponents could put renewed pressure on its human rights record. 

Al Jazeera's
